## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving its cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Add periodic-table element selection to the plate, evidence-informed reaction outcomes, and successful-result feedback with a name, badge, and description.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Provide detailed element and reaction information, with successful outcomes shown by name, badge, and description.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies, not biological predictions; make the DNA guide curated rather than exhaustive.

## Decisions
- Cell mechanics are educational proxies, not biological predictions.
- “All the DNA IRL know” means a curated educational guide, not an exhaustive database.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Browser validation confirmed Codex unlock, XP awards and level progression, reload and new-world persistence, and no horizontal overflow at 390px.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass; browser console showed no errors.
- Gathered OpenStax references for cellular respiration, magnesium as an enzyme cofactor, phosphorus in nucleic acids, and iron in hemoglobin.

### Active
- Add periodic-table element selection to the plate.
- Implement evidence-informed reaction outcomes and detailed success results with a name, badge, and description.

### Blocked
- Reaction-specific biological claims still need adequate supporting sources; prior searches did not provide sufficient source material.

## Next Move
1. Inspect plate state, rendering, action handling, and result UI in `app.js` and `style.css`.
2. Design a clearly educational element/reaction model with appropriately scoped, sourced information; integrate element selection and reaction feedback.
3. Validate interactions, persistence, responsiveness, and simulation behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Plate and cell simulation, research rewards, Codex content and views, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Codex navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `style.css`: Plate, Codex, progress, and responsive styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- `codexUnlocked()` requires at least one plate cell and one recorded research success; XP thresholds rise by 100 per level.
- `app.js` uses `makePlateState()`, `cellView()`, `handleAction()`, and delegated click handling for plate interactions.

- `labView()` configures experiments against `S.genome`; `runLab()` computes and records results; `resultMarkup()` displays them. `runLab()` guards DNA/RNA-dependent protocols based on sample state.

- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving its cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Add periodic-table element selection to the plate, evidence-informed reaction outcomes, and successful-result feedback with a name, badge, and description.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Provide detailed element and reaction information, with successful outcomes shown by name, badge, and description.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies, not biological predictions; make the DNA guide curated rather than exhaustive.

## Decisions
- Cell mechanics are educational proxies, not biological predictions.
- “All the DNA IRL know” means a curated educational guide, not an exhaustive database.
- Element selections should provide sourced educational context, not imply a modeled chemical reaction or cell response.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Browser validation confirmed Codex unlock, XP awards and level progression, reload and new-world persistence, and no horizontal overflow at 390px.
- Prior validation: `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass; browser console showed no errors.
- Added a periodic-table element dataset, group/period placement metadata, and sourced educational entries for C, N, O, Na, Mg, P, K, and Fe in `app.js`.

### Active
- Integrate the periodic table and element selection into the observatory plate.
- Show a relevant educational result card with outcome name, badge, description, and source; avoid implying biological predictions.
- Validate element interactions, persistence, responsiveness, and existing simulation behavior.

### Blocked
- Reaction-specific biological claims lack adequate supporting sources; keep outcomes scoped to supported educational connections rather than claiming simulated reactions.

## Next Move
1. Add plate UI for choosing elements from the periodic table and viewing element details.
2. Connect selection to an evidence-informed outcome card, using sourced entries where available and neutral educational context otherwise.
3. Validate interactions and run syntax, diff, and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Element dataset and guide entries; plate rendering, state, and delegated interactions.
- `style.css`: Plate and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- New `ELEMENTS`, `PERIODIC_ROWS`, `ELEMENT_POSITIONS`, and `ELEMENT_GUIDE` constants were added to `app.js`; table interaction and rendering are not yet integrated.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving its cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate periodic-table element selection into the observatory plate with sourced educational outcomes, without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Provide detailed element and outcome information, including a name, badge, description, and source.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selections provide educational context, not a modeled chemical reaction or cell response.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Added `ELEMENTS`, `PERIODIC_ROWS`, `ELEMENT_POSITIONS`, and sourced `ELEMENT_GUIDE` entries for C, N, O, Na, Mg, P, K, and Fe in `app.js`.

### Active
- Integrate the periodic table and element selection into the observatory plate.
- Show a relevant educational result card with outcome name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Validate element interactions, persistence, responsiveness, and existing simulation behavior.

### Blocked
- Reaction-specific biological claims lack adequate supporting sources; keep outcomes scoped to supported educational connections.

## Next Move
1. Add periodic-table UI and element selection to the observatory plate.
2. Connect selection to sourced guide entries or neutral educational context without changing simulated cell state.
3. Validate selection, persistence, responsive layout, and existing simulation behavior; run syntax, diff, and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Element datasets and guide entries; plate rendering, state, and delegated interactions.
- `style.css`: Plate and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- The periodic-table constants and guide have been added, but table rendering and interactions are not integrated.
- `S.env.chemical` is a generic chemical-stress value, not an element model.
- `runLab()` configures and records experiments; `resultMarkup()` renders results.
- OpenStax references in `ELEMENT_GUIDE`: https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/31-1-nutritional-requirements-of-plants, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-1-energy-in-living-systems, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/6-5-enzymes, https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/2-3-biological-molecules, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/39-4-transport-of-gases-in-human-bodily-fluids, and https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/5-3-active-transport.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving its cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate periodic-table element selection into the observatory plate with sourced educational outcomes, without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Provide detailed element and outcome information, including a name, badge, description, and source.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selections provide educational context, not a modeled chemical reaction or cell response.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Added `ELEMENTS`, `PERIODIC_ROWS`, `ELEMENT_POSITIONS`, and sourced `ELEMENT_GUIDE` entries for C, N, O, Na, Mg, P, K, and Fe in `app.js`.

### Active
- Integrate periodic-table UI and element selection into the observatory plate.
- Show a relevant educational result card with outcome name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Validate element interactions, persistence, responsiveness, and existing simulation behavior.

### Blocked
- Reaction-specific biological claims lack adequate supporting sources; keep outcomes scoped to supported educational connections.

## Next Move
1. Add periodic-table UI and element selection to the observatory plate.
2. Connect selection to sourced guide entries or neutral educational context without changing simulated cell state.
3. Validate selection, persistence, responsive layout, and existing simulation behavior; run syntax, diff, and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Element datasets and guide entries; plate rendering, state, and delegated interactions.
- `style.css`: Plate and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- Periodic-table constants and guide exist, but table rendering and interactions are not integrated.
- `S.env.chemical` is a generic chemical-stress value, not an element model.
- `runLab()` configures and records experiments; `resultMarkup()` renders results.
- OpenStax references in `ELEMENT_GUIDE`: https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/31-1-nutritional-requirements-of-plants, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-1-energy-in-living-systems, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/6-5-enzymes, https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/2-3-biological-molecules, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/39-4-transport-of-gases-in-human-bodily-fluids, and https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/5-3-active-transport.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving the cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate a periodic table into the observatory plate with sourced educational outcomes, without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; elements without guide entries get neutral context.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selection provides educational context only; it must not change simulated cell state or imply chemical reactions.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Added `ELEMENTS`, `PERIODIC_ROWS`, `ELEMENT_POSITIONS`, `ELEMENT_GUIDE`, and a periodic-table source reference in `app.js`.

### Active
- Integrate periodic-table rendering and element selection into the observatory plate.
- Show a relevant educational result card with outcome name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Validate element interactions, persistence, responsiveness, and existing simulation behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish adding periodic table and educational result card to the `cellView()` markup.
2. Persist element selection and add delegated click handling for `[data-element]`.
3. Validate element selection, persistence, responsive layout, and existing simulation behavior; run syntax, diff, and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Element datasets, `periodicTableMarkup()`, `elementResultMarkup()`, plate view, state, and delegated interactions.
- `style.css`: Plate and responsive styling; periodic-table and result-card styles still need adding.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- `periodicTableMarkup()` and `elementResultMarkup()` have been added but are not yet called from `cellView()`.
- Selection migration initializes `S.selectedElement` to `C`; selection persistence and click handling are still pending.
- `S.env.chemical` is a generic chemical-stress value, not an element model.
- `runLab()` configures and records experiments; `resultMarkup()` renders results.
- OpenStax guide references include `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/31-1-nutritional-requirements-of-plants`, `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-1-energy-in-living-systems`, `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/6-5-enzymes`, `https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/2-3-biological-molecules`, `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/39-4-transport-of-gases-in-human-bodily-fluids`, and `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/5-3-active-transport`.
- Neutral fallback citation: `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving the cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate an educational periodic table into the observatory plate without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; elements without guide entries get neutral context.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selection provides educational context only; it must not change simulated cell state or imply chemical reactions.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Added `ELEMENTS`, `PERIODIC_ROWS`, `ELEMENT_POSITIONS`, `ELEMENT_GUIDE`, and a periodic-table source reference in `app.js`.
- Added `periodicTableMarkup()` and `elementResultMarkup()`; initialized `S.selectedElement` to a valid element, defaulting to `C`.

### Active
- Integrate periodic-table and educational result-card markup into `cellView()`.
- Persist element selections and add delegated click handling for `[data-element]`.
- Add periodic-table/result-card styling and validate element interactions, persistence, responsiveness, and existing simulation behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add `periodicTableMarkup()` and `elementResultMarkup()` to the observatory plate view in `app.js`.
2. Add selection handling and persistence for `[data-element]`; style the table and result card in `style.css`.
3. Run syntax, diff, and browser checks, including interaction, persistence, responsiveness, and simulation regression checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Element datasets, periodic-table and result-card markup, plate view, state, and delegated interactions.
- `style.css`: Existing plate and responsive styling; periodic-table and result-card styles are pending.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- `periodicTableMarkup()` and `elementResultMarkup()` exist but are not yet called from `cellView()`.
- Element selection persistence and click handling are still pending; `S.selectedElement` currently initializes to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` is a generic chemical-stress value, not an element model.
- `runLab()` configures and records experiments; `resultMarkup()` renders results.
- OpenStax guide references include `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/31-1-nutritional-requirements-of-plants`, `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/7-1-energy-in-living-systems`, `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/6-5-enzymes`, `https://openstax.org/books/concepts-biology/pages/2-3-biological-molecules`, `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/39-4-transport-of-gases-in-human-bodily-fluids`, and `https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/5-3-active-transport`.
- Neutral fallback citation: `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving the cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate an educational periodic table into the observatory plate without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; elements without guide entries get neutral context.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selection provides educational context only; it must not change simulated cell state or imply chemical reactions.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, and ATP costs.
- Updated cell readings, organelle details, plate summaries, tooltips, staining, and visual indicators.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked and unlocked views, and source-plus-success access gating.
- Added researcher XP/level UI and state migration; successful lab protocols and genome sequencing award XP and show feedback.
- Researcher progress persists across reloads and new worlds.
- Added Codex, progress, and responsive styling; updated `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Added `ELEMENTS`, `PERIODIC_ROWS`, `ELEMENT_POSITIONS`, `ELEMENT_GUIDE`, and the periodic-table source reference in `app.js`.
- Integrated the periodic table and educational result card into `cellView()`.
- Added delegated `[data-element]` selection handling and persistence via `storeState()`.
- Added responsive table and element-result styling.

### Active
- Validate rendered table, selection behavior, persistence, responsiveness, and simulation regression behavior in a browser.

### Blocked
- Browser check is inconclusive: the probe HTML was written to `/tmp/opencode`, so its relative `app.js` path did not load; it reported `rendered tiles=0` and failed to find `[data-view="cell"]`.

## Next Move
1. Run browser checks from the repository directory (or otherwise preserve relative asset paths) and verify element selection, result-card source/context, and persisted selection.
2. Check mobile/table responsiveness and confirm selecting elements does not affect simulation state.
3. Review `git diff` and existing simulation behavior; `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Periodic-table data, markup, observatory view, selection handling, and state persistence.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table/result-card and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: App navigation and researcher progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` is a generic chemical-stress value, not an element model.
- Neutral fallback citation: `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving its cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate an educational periodic table into the cell observatory without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selection is informational only and must not change simulated cell state or imply chemical reactions.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked/unlocked views, source-plus-success access gating, researcher XP/levels, and progress persistence.
- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI, educational result card, delegated element selection, persistence, and responsive styling.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed in earlier checks.
- Browser probe confirmed 118 element tiles, Oganesson selection and neutral context/source, and persisted selected element. A later expanded probe produced malformed output and needs rerunning to verify simulation invariance and mobile layout.

### Active
- Finish browser validation of element selection persistence, unchanged simulation state, and mobile responsiveness.
- Review the full diff and determine whether `genesis-latest.jpeg` reflects the latest UI.

### Blocked
- The latest probe output was malformed (`${out.join(...)}` appeared literally), so simulation-state comparison and responsive layout checks remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Fix and rerun `.genesis-browser-probe.html` so it reports selection persistence, simulation-state comparison, periodic-table scroll dimensions, and document overflow at a 390px viewport.
2. Remove `.genesis-browser-probe.html` after validation.
3. Review `git diff`, confirm whether `genesis-latest.jpeg` is current, then rerun `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation, periodic-table data/rendering/selection/persistence, Codex, and researcher progression.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, element-result, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot; latest UI correspondence is unconfirmed.
- `.genesis-browser-probe.html`: Temporary browser test page; remove after validation.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- Persistence key is `genesis-living-genome-v1`; `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` is generic chemical stress, not an element model.
- Neutral fallback citation is `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.
- A server already responds at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; attempting to start another failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex and researcher progression while preserving its cell-state and checkpoint simulation.
- Integrate an educational periodic table into the cell observatory without implying modeled chemical reactions or biological predictions.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selection is informational only and must not change simulated cell state or imply chemical reactions.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, locked/unlocked views, source-plus-success access gating, researcher XP/levels, and progress persistence.
- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI, educational result card, element selection, persistence, and responsive styling.
- Earlier checks passed: `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Browser probe previously confirmed 118 element tiles, Oganesson selection with neutral context/source, and persisted selection.

### Active
- Validate selection persistence, simulation-state invariance, and mobile responsiveness with a working browser probe.
- Review the full diff and determine whether `genesis-latest.jpeg` reflects the latest UI.

### Blocked
- The latest probe still outputs the template literally (`${out.join('...')}`), so simulation-state comparison and responsive layout checks remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Fix `.genesis-browser-probe.html` so the result template interpolates correctly, then rerun it at a 390px viewport to check selection persistence, unchanged simulation state, periodic-table scroll dimensions, and document overflow.
2. Remove `.genesis-browser-probe.html` after validation.
3. Review `git diff`, confirm whether `genesis-latest.jpeg` is current, then rerun `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation, periodic-table data/rendering/selection/persistence, Codex, and researcher progression.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, element-result, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot; latest UI correspondence is unconfirmed.
- `.genesis-browser-probe.html`: Temporary browser test page; fix and remove after validation.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- Persistence key is `genesis-living-genome-v1`; `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` is generic chemical stress, not an element model.
- Neutral fallback citation is `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex, researcher progression, and an informational periodic table integrated into the cell observatory while preserving the existing simulation.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.
- Element selection is informational only and must not change simulated cell state or imply chemical reactions.

## Decisions
- Describe element connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for the simulated cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, source-plus-success access gating, researcher XP/levels, and progress persistence.
- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI, educational result card, element selection, and persistence.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` completed without reported errors.
- A 390px browser viewport was confirmed with no document horizontal overflow; this run did not find element tiles, so selection and periodic-table behavior remain unverified at that viewport.

### Active
- Investigate why the 390px browser run found `tileCount: 0` after navigating to the cell observatory; then verify selection persistence and simulation-state invariance at 390px.
- Review whether `genesis-latest.jpeg` reflects the latest UI.
- Remove temporary `.genesis-browser-probe.html` after validation.

### Blocked
- Responsive periodic-table and selection checks are incomplete because the 390px run returned `tileCount: 0` and `selectionPersisted: false`.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose the 390px browser probe’s navigation/rendering and rerun checks for all 118 tiles, selection persistence, simulation-state invariance, periodic-table scroll dimensions, and document overflow.
2. Remove `.genesis-browser-probe.html`.
3. Review the diff and screenshot correspondence; rerun `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation, periodic-table behavior and persistence, Codex, and researcher progression.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, element-result, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot; correspondence to latest UI is unconfirmed.
- `.genesis-browser-probe.html`: Temporary browser test page; untracked and pending removal.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted; `.genesis-browser-probe.html` is untracked.
- Persistence key is `genesis-living-genome-v1`; `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` is generic chemical stress, not an element model.
- Neutral fallback citation is `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.
- Server responds at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.
- The earlier 500px probe confirmed 118 tiles, persistent Oganesson selection, neutral context/source, and unchanged simulation state; it did not confirm mobile layout.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex, researcher progression, and an informational periodic table integrated into the cell observatory while preserving the existing simulation.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex, researcher progression, and periodic table, and let players add selected elements to the plate and observe cell responses.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Let players add an element to the plate and see the cell react.
- Treat cell mechanics as educational proxies and the DNA guide as curated, not exhaustive.

## Decisions
- Describe cell-mechanic connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for a real cell.
- Use evidence-supported educational connections and avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.

- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI, educational result card, element selection, and persistence.
- Verified all 118 elements render; at 390px the table scrolls within its container without document horizontal overflow.
- Verified Og selection persists and does not change simulation state.
- Refreshed `genesis-latest.jpeg`; removed `.genesis-browser-probe.html`.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Implement plate addition for selected elements and model an educational cell response to those additions.

- (none)

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex, researcher progression, and periodic table, and let players add selected elements to the plate and observe cell responses.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA material hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Element selections show a name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Let players add an element to the plate and see the cell react.
- Treat cell-mechanic connections as educational examples, not predicted outcomes for a real cell; the DNA guide is curated, not exhaustive.

## Decisions
- Use evidence-supported educational connections and avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- Provide neutral educational context for elements without specific guide entries.
- Element selection is currently informational only; it does not change the selected cell or simulation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, source-plus-success access gating, researcher XP/levels, and progress persistence.
- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI with educational result cards, element selection, and persistence.
- Verified all 118 elements render; at 390px the table scrolls within its container without document horizontal overflow.
- Verified Og selection persists without changing simulation state.
- Refreshed `genesis-latest.jpeg`; removed `.genesis-browser-probe.html`.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Implement plate addition for selected elements and a cautious educational response model with UI feedback.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add an element-to-plate interaction in the periodic-table result UI.
2. Model a limited, clearly educational response to adding an element and display the selected cell’s response; avoid implying real biological predictions.
3. Persist the addition and verify the resulting UI and simulation behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation, cell-plate state and rendering, element data/selection/persistence, Codex, and researcher progression.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, element-result, plate, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- Persistence key is `genesis-living-genome-v1`; `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` is generic chemical stress, not an element model.
- Neutral fallback citation is `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.
- `cellView()` renders the periodic table and result card; `handleAction()` handles plate interactions; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell metrics.

  `S` is initialized from `loadState()` or `initialState(...)`, then normalized in place. Add exposure state alongside `S.selectedElement` and validate/default it during this normalization.

- **Persistence — `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:50–51`**  
  `storeState()` saves all `S` properties except `playing`; `loadState()` restores the stored object. A new property on `S` is therefore persisted automatically. Note that `newWorld()` creates fresh state and explicitly carries over research progress, so choose whether exposures should reset or be preserved there (`:96`).

- **Record exposures — `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:118`**  
  The delegated document click handler handles `[data-element]`: it updates `S.selectedElement`, calls `storeState()`, then `render()`. This is the existing pattern to extend for recording an exposure when an element is selected.

- **Display — `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:85–87`**  
  `periodicTableMarkup()` renders the tiles; `elementResultMarkup()` renders the selected-element result; `cellView()` combines them inside `.periodic-card`. These are the natural places to show exposure counts or history.

- **Styling — `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css:1`**  
  The stylesheet is densely packed onto lines. Add styles alongside the existing periodic-result selectors (`.element-result`, `.element-result-symbol`, `.element-result-copy`); existing cards and metrics use `.card`, `.metric-strip`, and `.metric-card`.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex, researcher progression, and periodic table, including a cautious way to add selected elements to a plate and observe a cell response.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA content hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Show selected-element name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Let players add an element to the plate and observe a cell response.
- Present cell-mechanic connections as educational examples, not real-cell predictions; clarify that the DNA guide is curated, not exhaustive.

## Decisions
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- For elements without guide entries, show neutral periodic-table context.
- Element exposure markers are persistent, visual-only annotations with a brief halo; they do not represent dose or alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, source-plus-success access gating, researcher XP/levels, and progress persistence.
- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI; all 118 elements render, and the table scrolls within its container on mobile without document horizontal overflow.
- Added persistent per-cell element markers, selected-cell marker counts, plate-cell indicators, and a brief visual halo on addition.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass; browser loaded the observatory and showed the add-element control.

### Active
- Exercise the add-marker interaction in-browser and verify persistence after reload and cell reselection.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Click “Add [symbol] to plate”; confirm the selected cell’s marker count and visual response update.
2. Reload and verify the marker persists; select another cell to confirm its count is separate.
3. Refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if the final UI changes warrant an updated screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation, cell-plate state and rendering, element markers/persistence, Codex, researcher progression.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, element-result, plate, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- Persistence key is `genesis-living-genome-v1`; `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` remains generic chemical stress; element markers do not feed into it or other cell metrics.
- Neutral fallback citation is `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.
- `cellView()` renders the periodic table and result card; `handleAction()` handles plate interactions.
- Browser check opened the cell observatory and confirmed 12 cells and an add-element control; the marker action and persistence have not yet been exercised.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with an educational DNA Codex, researcher progression, and periodic table, including a cautious way to add selected elements to a plate and observe a cell response.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA content hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Show selected-element name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Let players add an element to the plate and observe a cell response.
- Present cell-mechanic connections as educational examples, not real-cell predictions; clarify that the DNA guide is curated, not exhaustive.

## Decisions
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- For elements without guide entries, show neutral periodic-table context.
- Element markers are persistent, visual-only annotations with a brief halo; they do not represent dose or alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cell oxidative stress, protein-folding load, membrane integrity, cell-state transitions, checkpoint-gated division, daughter-cell variation, ATP costs, and related UI.
- Added Codex navigation, curated articles, source-plus-success access gating, researcher XP/levels, and progress persistence.
- Added periodic-table data and observatory UI; all 118 elements render, and the table scrolls within its container on mobile without document horizontal overflow.
- Added persistent per-cell element markers, selected-cell marker counts, plate-cell indicators, and a brief visual halo on addition.
- Browser-verified adding a marker to `CELL-001`, persistence after reload, and separation from `CELL-002`.
- Refreshed `genesis-latest.jpeg`; `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation, cell-plate state and rendering, element markers/persistence, Codex, researcher progression.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, element-result, plate, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are uncommitted.
- Persistence key is `genesis-living-genome-v1`; `S.selectedElement` defaults to `C` if unset or invalid.
- `S.env.chemical` remains generic chemical stress; element markers do not feed into it or other cell metrics.
- Neutral fallback citation is `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.
- `cellView()` renders the periodic table and result card; `handleAction()` handles plate interactions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify GENESIS’s DNA Codex, researcher progression, and periodic-table features, then clean and check the code and clear saved data.

## Requirements
- Keep curated DNA content hidden until a source is on the plate and research succeeds.
- Award XP for successful lab protocols and genome sequencing; allow uncapped level progression.
- Show selected-element name, badge, description, and source; provide neutral context for elements without guide entries.
- Let players add an element to the plate and observe a cell response.
- Present cell-mechanic connections as educational examples, not real-cell predictions; clarify that the DNA guide is curated, not exhaustive.
- Element markers are visual-only annotations, not doses, and must not alter cell metrics.

## Decisions
- Use evidence-supported educational connections; avoid unsupported reaction-specific biological claims.
- For elements without guide entries, show neutral periodic-table context.
- Element markers persist per cell and trigger a brief halo without changing cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented cell mechanics, Codex access gating, researcher progression, 118 periodic-table elements, and per-cell element markers.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed a fresh initial view, locked Codex, 12 plate cells, and no document horizontal overflow before the test script stopped.

### Active
- Finish Chromium verification of element details and markers, lab XP and sequencing XP, Codex unlock/content, and high-level progression.
- Clear saved data; this remains unconfirmed.

### Blocked
- The browser test stopped at its first assertion: after removing local storage and reloading, the new state had not yet been persisted, so the expected `plate` value was missing. Remaining browser checks did not run.

## Next Move
1. Adjust the browser test to account for fresh state being persisted only after interaction, then run the remaining feature checks.
2. Clear the intended saved data and confirm it is gone.
3. Rerun syntax and diff checks and report any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation state, persistence, periodic table, Codex, XP, and interactions.
- `style.css`: Periodic-table, plate, Codex, and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher-progress markup.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Updated observatory screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Persistence key: `genesis-living-genome-v1`; selected element defaults to `C`.
- Neutral periodic-table source: `https://www.rsc.org/periodic-table`.
- Element markers do not feed into chemical stress or other cell metrics.
